name: production-ready
title: Production-ready audit
description: Judges the change against a production bar with per-criterion verdicts: behavior, security and data-handling are blocking; performance, observability, docs and accessibility are nudges. Fails only when a blocking criterion is unmet. Promote it into the default reviews by copying it to ~/.tower/flows with "when": ["after-tests"].

steps.name: audit
steps.text:
Decide whether this change is ready to run in production, criterion by criterion — not whether it is elegant. The card: {{title}}.

{{brief}}

Read the diff against the base branch, and the plan at `{{planPath}}` if it exists. Judge seven criteria, each with its own verdict and one grounded justification quoting the code:

Blocking — the change does not ship until met. Behavior: does what the card says, and the edge cases the brief names are handled. Security: the new surface's trust boundaries are checked; no new injection, secret, or permission risk. Data: writes are valid, migrations are reversible, nothing crosses tenants or users.

Nudges — worth saying, never worth blocking. Performance: obviously wasteful paths only. Observability: would an on-call engineer see this fail. Docs: does a future reader have what they need. Accessibility: if user-facing.

Write the audit to the absolute path `{{reportPath}}` as a seven-row table: criterion, verdict (met / unmet / n-a), evidence, and for each unmet blocking row the one change that would meet it. Fail the stage only if a BLOCKING criterion is unmet; pass otherwise, with the nudges named in your summary. A criterion that does not apply to this change is n-a, not unmet.
